# Intake Brief — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR)

**Headline:** Add a dedicated, auto-discovered `GymPowerUpLeveling` demonstration
scene that makes every power-up's (P3–P10) run-scoped level curve observable —
field pickups and hold-full permanent rewards both level the power-up up, and a
live readout shows the resolver-derived stats — plus integration and
game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared power-up
level path is byte-for-byte the same in `PlayScene` and the gyms.

## Problem statement

The power-up level model, resolver and store are shipped
(`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and wired into the
shared effect path and every scene (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K, AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB,
AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9), but there is **no dedicated place to see and verify it**
the way weapons have `GymWeaponLeveling`. The existing power-up gyms
(`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) demonstrate behaviours, not levels;
the parity tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boot a
*minimal* `EquivGymScene`, not a real gym, and only exercise a single power-up
(P5). There is therefore a gap in both **legibility** (a producer/designer
cannot watch a power-up level up and see its stats change) and **verification**
(no test proves a shipped gym resolves the level path identically to the game).

## Users

- **Designer / producer (legibility):** "As a designer, I want a gym where I can
  collect a power-up repeatedly and watch its level and resolved stats change,
  so I can sanity-check the curve without reading the catalogue."
- **Engineer (verification):** "As an engineer, I want a test that boots the real
  gym and the game and proves they resolve the same level path for every
  power-up, so a divergent copy cannot slip through."
- **Player (indirect):** "As a player, I want the power-up levels I earn to be
  applied identically everywhere they appear, with no gym-only behaviour."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Dedicated gym scene.** A new `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
  (scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, conventional `Gym<Name>.ts` so it is
  auto-discovered by `GymIndex` with no index edit) demonstrates the level
  curve of **every** power-up P3–P10: the operator can collect each power-up
  repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward, and the scene
  shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all
  catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats only through the
  shared `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (and `EffectsRegistry`);
  it defines no copy of the curve, the catalogue or the level arithmetic, and
  introduces no new shared helper or template-method copy (the duplicate-body
  guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass).
- **AC3 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`
  drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling,
  hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade /
  mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run
  restart.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` alongside
  `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep
  (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, the resolved stats and the observable
  effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7
  teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical. The parity assertion lives in the
  shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body
  guard convention is respected.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The GDD §4.4.3 status paragraph, the README power-up
  leveling entry and the "Coverage:" lists name the new gym and its tests
  (and any code comments added are accurate).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** An enabled gameplay object must run the same
  code in a gym and the game; any behaviour shared by game and gym lives once in
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both. No divergent copy.
- **Demonstration only.** This item adds a scene and tests; it must **not**
  change gameplay balance, tuning or the level catalogue. Any balance change
  discovered is a separate linked work item, not scope creep.
- **Auto-discovery convention.** New gym is `src/scenes/gym/Gym<Name>.ts`; the
  scene key equals the class name.
- **Deterministic tests.** Scene tests use the `bootScene` harness and the public
  `tick(dt)` entry point (no real render loop), matching the existing gym tests;
  generous Vitest timeouts are acceptable for Phaser boot.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and work-item text.

## Existing state

- **Model shipped:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`
  (all P3–P10), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`,
  run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` on `Player` (`getPowerUpLevel`,
  `getPowerUpLevels`, `resetPowerUpLevels`), shared curve in
  `src/utils/curve.ts`.
- **Effect path wired:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` consumes the player's
  store; P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` axes wired;
  hold-full `ChoiceContext.powerUpLevels` + `power-up-level` offers applied via
  shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- **Precedent:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) is the
  weapon-leveling demonstration gym (parent AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J); `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers gyms; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the DOM-panel readout pattern.
- **Existing power-up gyms:** `GymPowerUpsCombat` (P3/P4/P6/P7, threats) and
  `GymPowerUpsUtility` (P5/P8/P9/P10, threat-free) demonstrate behaviour, not
  levels; neither shows a level/stat readout.
- **Existing partial parity:** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boots a minimal
  `EquivGymScene` and checks P5 only; `PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` covers
  the choice path in the game.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) renders weapon levels but has no power-up level
  readout.

## Desired change

Add `GymPowerUpLeveling` (auto-discovered) as the canonical place to observe
every power-up's level curve, showing level and resolver-derived stats; add
integration tests for field-pickup and hold-full leveling, the readout and
run-restart reset; and add game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and
assert the shared level path matches `PlayScene` for every power-up. Update the
GDD/README references accordingly. No gameplay behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — **new** demonstration gym scene:
  round-robin/level-up drop source for P3–P10, hold-full permanent path, and a
  level + resolved-stats readout (reusing the shared store/resolver).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — **new** integration tests
  (field pickup, permanent reward, readout vs resolver, reset-on-restart,
  every-power-up-has-an-axis).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend (or add a sibling
  real-gym parity test) to boot `GymPowerUpLeveling` and assert
  `PlayScene`↔gym identity across every power-up and a level sweep; keeps the
  duplicate-body guard authoritative.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **read-only** shared source of truth
  (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStore`); do not
  duplicate.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — shared effect path consumed by the gym (read-only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — only if a power-up level readout is added to the shared HUD;
  otherwise the readout stays gym-local (e.g. a `.gym-panel`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 — update the status/coverage sentence to
  name the shipped gym + tests.
- `README.md` — update the power-up leveling entry and its Coverage list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (primary):** a demo gym invites "while we're here" gameplay
  or tuning changes. Mitigation: this item is demonstration + tests only; record
  any balance/behaviour opportunity as a separate `discovered-from` item.
- **Threats vs legibility (assumption):** P3/P4/P6/P7 are only fully observable
  under threat; the demonstration gym may include an optional threat toggle
  **or** focus on the resolver/level readout and leave full combat behaviour to
  `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Chosen default: threat-free readout gallery, with an
  optional threat toggle only if needed for the parity tests.
- **HUD coupling (assumption):** the shared HUD has no power-up level readout;
  keep the new readout gym-local to avoid changing shared HUD behaviour.
- **Parity-test flakiness (risk):** booting two Phaser games per case under
  parallel load is slow; reuse the existing generous timeout pattern and a
  single level sweep per power-up rather than many boots.
- **Reset-on-run-restart (ambiguity):** the gym must offer a deterministic way
  to exercise `resetPowerUpLevels` for the reset test; expose a public
  restart/reset hook (test-only seam) rather than relying on a real GameOver.
- **Determinism (constraint):** all tests drive `tick(dt)`, no wall-clock.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Design level curves for all power-ups (parent /
  `discovered-from`). Ships the model this gym demonstrates.
- **AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Wire power-up level curves into `EffectsRegistry`
  and the shared effect path (predecessor; makes field pickups level up).
- **AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB** — Wire P3 shield absorption and P4 periodic bomb
  (range/frequency) level axes into the effect path.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** — Integrate power-up level-up offers into the
  hold-full choice.
- **AH-0MUWGD0EN008T3TY** — P4 model: `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` replace
  `bombCharges` (supersedes the original P4 axis).
- **AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J** — Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration
  tests (the direct structural precedent; mirrors the same shape for weapons).
- **AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA** — Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining
  core-code duplication (the parity convention this item must respect).
- **AH-0MUTPEIN0000MDUR** — Test: P10 parity across `PlayScene`, `GymMinerals`
  and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (precedent for real-gym parity tests).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** – Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies) (completed)
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** – Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed)
- **AH-0MU44MAAB0007BDD** – Documentation for combat spawning (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, assert, body (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, applies, assert, body, combatscene (+20 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, body, combatscene (+20 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was conducted: the seed context plus the
shipped model, the wiring predecessors and the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
were sufficient to draft a clear brief (intake SKILL §4 — skip the interview
when seed context suffices; AGENTS.md — do not ask unnecessary questions). Each
apparent design choice is recorded below with the evidence that resolved it and
the documented assumption taken where evidence was partial.

- **Q (resolved from the work item + precedent): Should this be a new dedicated
  gym or an extension of `GymPowerUpsCombat` / `GymPowerUpsUtility`?**
  — Answer: a **new** `GymPowerUpLeveling` scene. Evidence: the work-item title
  and description say "Add a gym scene"; the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
  (AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J) established a dedicated leveling gym; `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers `Gym<Name>.ts`. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- **Q (resolved from the work item): What is the parity-test scope?**
  — Answer: boot the **real** gym and assert the shared power-up level path is
  identical to `PlayScene`, not another minimal `EquivGymScene`. Evidence: the
  description explicitly requires game↔gym parity "for the shared power-up level
  path" and names the duplicate-body guard. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): Should the gym include combat threats so P3/P4/P6/P7
  behaviour is fully observable?**
  — Answer (assumed, producer may override): threat-free readout gallery as the
  default, with an optional threat toggle only if the parity tests require
  observable combat behaviour. Evidence: `GymWeaponLeveling` is threat-free and
  demonstrates levels via a readout; `GymPowerUpsCombat` already owns the
  threat-based P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour. Source: `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): What demonstrates "level" — a shared HUD readout or
  a gym-local panel?**
  — Answer (assumed): gym-local readout over `PowerUpLevelStore` /
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`; avoid changing shared HUD behaviour. Evidence: the
  shared HUD has only a weapon-level readout; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the
  established gym-local `.gym-panel` pattern. Source: `src/ui/HUD.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): How does the gym exercise level reset?**
  — Answer (assumed): expose a deterministic public restart/reset hook on the
  gym scene so the reset test does not depend on a real GameOver sequence.
  Source: `Player.getPowerUpLevels` / `resetPowerUpLevels`
  (`src/entities/Player.ts`).
- **Observation:** the automated `find-related` report surfaced only generic
  matches (enemy gym, difficulty curve, combat-spawning docs); the higher-signal
  relationships above were found by manual worklog search and file inspection.

# Scripted Gameplay Videos (Multi-Scene Capture)

In a scripted video capture we create a level, play it for x seconds, then capture y seconds, pause the video capture. Create a new level, play it for x seconds, capture y seconds. There should be a fade to black and a fade from black lasting 0.25 seconds between each scene. There are an arbitrary number of scenes.

## Problem statement

The current capture system produces a single continuous video — either one full demo run with tail, or a fixed-length scripted clip. This feature adds **multi-scene** capture: sequence several gameplay segments (levels or gyms), play each for a configured duration, capture each for a configured duration, and stitch them into one video with fade transitions (0.25 s black fade in/out) between scenes.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can define a sequence of scenes and capture each one with play/capture durations and fade transitions, producing a single compiled video showing multiple gameplay segments for demo / showcase / marketing purposes.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants to create showcase videos that demonstrate several distinct gameplay elements (different gyms, boss phases, power-up interactions) in one compiled video, rather than multiple separate recordings.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — single-scene capture orchestrator
- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — scripted bot plan + probe helpers
- `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` — run-end signal, tail/cap logic
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — hermetic tests
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documentation
- `src/scenes/gym/` — individual gym scenes (each exercises one mechanic), discovered dynamically via `import.meta.glob`
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — dev gym index (reached from the menu's "Gym Scene Index (dev)" control)
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — URL-selected dev scenarios (`boss-four-hits`, `boss`, `defeat`) with a page-side release handle
- No fade/transition or multi-scene stitching exists in capture tooling.

## Desired change

1. A capture mode that defines a **scene list** (via a config file — see Q1) — each entry specifying the target, play duration (x), and capture duration (y).
2. Between each scene, a **fade-to-black (0.25 s)** then **fade-from-black (0.25 s)** transition is rendered **page-side** and captured by the running recorder.
3. The final output is a **single stitched WebM** containing all scenes with transitions, written to the configured output path.

## Design decisions (producer answers)

- **Q1 — Scene-list specification:** **A (config file).** A JSON config file lists the scenes with their targets and play/capture durations.
- **Q3 — Fade rendering:** **A (page-side canvas overlay).** The fade is drawn over the canvas by the capture (Playwright injection), so the continuously-running `MediaRecorder` captures it and no game-side change is needed. Because one recorder runs across all scenes, scene switching must happen **in-page** (a page reload would end the recorder).
- **Q2 — Scene target:** OPEN — expanded analysis posted in the comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6` (options A gym scene keys / B dev scenarios / C generated game levels / D generic scene key; recommended A). Pending producer choice.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — new flags/mode for scene lists
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (new) — scene-list config parsing, batch orchestration, page-side fade overlay, and single-output stitching
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — new tests for scene parsing, fade timing, and stitch logic
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documentation
- `src/` — a small dev-gated page-side scene-start hook, if Q2 resolves to A/B/C/D (exact location depends on the Q2 answer)

## Open Questions (need producer review)

**Q2: What does each scene target, and how is it started?** — full analysis in comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6`:

- **A.** Gym scene keys (e.g. `GymPlayer`, `GymScout`, `GymWeapons`, `GymBoss`) — widest showcase variety, least per-scene work; dev-only scenes. *(Recommended)*
- **B.** Dev scenarios (e.g. `boss-four-hits`, `defeat`) — real gameplay but verification-oriented; each new variant is a `src/` change.
- **C.** Generated game levels (shipped `PlayScene`, fresh level per scene) — literal match to the brief; multi-wave, needs a dev hook.
- **D.** Arbitrary registered scene key — maximally flexible; best as the internal mechanism, not a separate feature.

## Appendix: Interview Q&A

- **Q1 (Map, to producer): Scene list specification?** — **ANSWERED:** **A** — JSON config file. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (Map, to producer): Scene target specification?** — **EXPANDED, OPEN.** Options and impacts posted in comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6` after producer asked for more detail. Recommended: A (gym scene keys).
- **Q3 (Map, to producer): Fade rendering method?** — **ANSWERED:** **A** — page-side canvas overlay via Playwright. Source: interactive reply.

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).

- If a change is recommended, follow-up implementation work items are created; otherwise the item is closed as 'no change required'.

## Problem

Running `npm run build` from a git worktree created by the implement skill fails at the `build-audio` step:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'tsx' imported from /home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules/toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js
```

## Root cause

`scripts/build-audio.mjs` `resolveToneForge()` resolves the sibling checkout as `join(repoRoot, '..', 'ToneForge')`. Inside a worktree (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`) that path is `.worklog/worktrees/ToneForge`, which does not exist, so resolution falls through to `tf` on PATH (`node_modules/.bin/tf -> ../toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js`). That copy has no `tsx` dependency, so the CLI crashes.

When built from the main checkout the sibling path resolves correctly and the build succeeds.

## Workaround used

`TONEFORGE_CLI=/home/rgardler/projects/ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js npm run build` (the sibling's `node_modules` has `tsx`).

## Expected behaviour

`npm run build` succeeds inside a worktree without requiring `TONEFORGE_CLI` to be set manually, since worktrees are the mandated implementation workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `npm run build` succeeds from a worktree with no `TONEFORGE_CLI` set.
- AC2: Sibling resolution is anchored to the main checkout (e.g. via the git common dir) rather than the worktree root.
- AC3: Existing `build-audio` tests still pass and the main-checkout build is unaffected.

## Summary

During a `dev`→`main` release (`/skill:ship release`), the audit-readiness gate's conservative in-gate remediation re-runs `audit_runner.py issue <id>` for a top-level `in_review` item whose stored audit is stale/missing/transient. For an item with a passing verdict the runner sets `needsProducerReview=yes` (by design, so the producer-review gate blocks until a human reviews).

The problem: if the item was **already producer-approved** (`needsProducerReview=false`) — the normal steady state after the producer has reviewed it — a content-unchanged re-audit nonetheless flips the flag back to `true` and immediately blocks the release at the producer-review gate (exit 9) and the final-validation sweep (exit 12).

## Example User Story

As a producer running a release, having already reviewed and approved every top-level work item, I want the release's automatic audit remediation not to re-open producer review for an item whose content I already approved, so that a stale audit does not silently re-block an otherwise shippable release.

## Observed

Release run on 2026-10-08 (AI_Hell, dev→main, v0.1.10 candidate):

- Item `AH-0MUZDXF2U001MJW1` (top-level `test-failure`, completed/in_review) had `needsProducerReview=false` for its **entire** recorded history (verified from the `refs/worklog/data` sync commits: false from creation 10:19 through the last pre-release sync at 11:16:27 UTC).
- The audit gate reported `auto-remediating AH-0MUZDXF2U001MJW1 (stale audit)` and `auto-remediated successfully` at 11:20:39 UTC.
- The producer-review gate then blocked with exit 9: `1 of 24 work item(s) need producer review`.
- `wl audit-show` confirms the fresh audit is green (`readyToClose: true`, content fingerprint unchanged).

## Expected Behaviour (candidate)

One or both of:

1. In-gate remediation should preserve an existing `needsProducerReview=false` approval when the item's content fingerprint is unchanged across the re-audit (only a genuine content change should re-open producer review); and/or
2. The producer-review gate should recognise a flag that was set by an in-gate remediation in the same run and not treat it as a fresh, un-reviewed requirement (e.g. compare against the pre-run approved state).

## Evidence / References

- `$(skill_path ship)/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (in-gate remediation re-runs the audit; "the gate never calls wl update directly").
- `$(skill_path ship)/scripts/audit-remediation.js` (bounded remediation; no flag preservation).
- `$(skill_path audit)/scripts/audit_runner.py` (~L11784: sets `--needs-producer-review yes` for top-level passing audits).
- Related: AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB (producer-review remediation hint flag casing).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A release whose only producer-review blocker is a flag set by the same run's in-gate audit remediation (item previously approved, content unchanged) does not fail the producer-review gate; verified by a unit test with injected `getCandidateItemsFn`/remediation boundaries.
2. If an item's content genuinely changed since its last audit, re-audit still re-opens producer review (the safety behaviour is preserved); verified by a unit test.
3. No regression in the existing producer-review gate tests (child override/escalation, `null`/`undefined` handling).
4. Documentation (ship skill reference) states whether a content-unchanged re-audit preserves the producer-review approval.

## Summary

During the v0.1.10 dev→main release, the ship skill's **non-blocking** post-release branch cleanup (run-release.js step 10, `runPostReleaseCleanup`) failed:

```
Post-release cleanup: enumerating branches...
  ⚠ Failed to read summarize report; skipping local cleanup.
Found 0 merged local branch(es) to clean up.
Post-release cleanup: pruning local branches...
  Pruned 0 local branch(es).
Post-release cleanup: pruning remote branches...
  ⚠ Remote branch pruning failed: delete_remote_branches.py failed
```

Re-running the same scripts manually immediately afterwards succeeded (`summarize_branches.py ~6s`, `delete_remote_branches.py ~6s`, both exit 0), so the failure is not a permanent environment problem.

## Likely Cause

`runPostReleaseCleanup` passes a **fixed** report path `${os.tmpdir()}/cleanup-summary.json` (`run-release.js` ~L735). In a multi-agent environment (herdr) where more than one agent may run a release/cleanup concurrently, the fixed path races: one process can truncate/replace the file while another reads it, producing the "Failed to read summarize report" path, and the follow-on remote prune inherits the broken state.

## Expected Behaviour

- The post-release cleanup uses a unique temporary report path (e.g. `mkdtempSync`) so concurrent runs cannot clobber each other.
- A transient cleanup failure is retried once, and the warning names the deterministic remediation.

## Evidence / References

- `$(skill_path ship)/scripts/run-release.js` `runPostReleaseCleanup` (fixed `${tempDir}/cleanup-summary.json`; `delete_remote_branches.py` invocation).
- `$(skill_path cleanup)/scripts/{summarize_branches,prune_local_branches,delete_remote_branches}.py` — all succeed standalone.
- Discovered during release v0.1.10 (`discovered-from:release-v0.1.10`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-release cleanup uses a unique temp path per run; a unit test with two concurrent-invocation fakes proves no shared-path clobber.
2. A failed `summarize_branches.py`/report read no longer silently reports "0 merged branches" as if the repo were clean — it logs a distinct, actionable warning.
3. The cleanup remains non-blocking (never changes the release exit code).

# Batch scenario / multi-video capture tooling

## Problem statement

`npm run capture` produces exactly one video per invocation, and `--scenario`
accepts a single, unlisted value. There is no way to (a) discover which dev
scenarios exist, (b) run every scenario in one call, or (c) generate N videos
without a shell loop that pays the Vite + Chromium startup cost on every run.

**User stories:**

- As the maintainer, I want `npm run capture -- --list-scenarios` to show every
  implemented dev scenario (name + one-line effect) so I do not have to read the
  source.
- As the maintainer, I want `npm run capture -- --all-scenarios` to produce one
  video per scenario in a single command, reusing one Vite server and one
  browser session.
- As the maintainer, I want `npm run capture -- --count N` (optionally with
  `--scenario`) to produce N videos as review / regression evidence.
- As a producer/reviewer, I want a final batch summary and a non-zero exit when
  any item fails, so a batch can gate CI.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` / `parseCaptureArgs`: a single `scenario`
  string; flags are `--duration`, `--tail`, `--max-duration`, `--warmup`,
  `--output`, `--port`, `--headed`, `--json`, `--keep-server`, `--scripted`,
  `--scenario`.
- `runCapture` boots one Vite dev server + one Chromium browser per invocation
  and writes one output WebM.
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` is the game-side resolver: `boss`, `boss-four-hits`,
  `defeat` (plus the default no-scenario demo run). The Node capture tool does
  not import it; `--scenario` is passed through the URL unvalidated (an unknown
  value silently runs the normal demo).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents the three scenario values in a table.
- There is no `--list-scenarios`, `--all-scenarios` or `--count`, and no shared
  scenario registry between the game and the Node tool.

## Desired change

1. **Scenario registry (single source).** Add a shared, pure scenario registry
   (name + short description) usable by both the game resolver and the Node
   capture tool, so the list cannot drift. Likely a browser-free `.mjs` module
   (mirroring `capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`) that `src/core/devScenario.ts`
   consumes.
2. **`--list-scenarios`.** Print the implemented scenarios in human-readable
   form, or machine-readable JSON with `--json`; exit 0 without booting
   Vite/Chromium.
3. **`--all-scenarios`.** Run every registered scenario in one invocation, one
   video each, continuing past a per-item failure and reporting a per-item plus
   aggregate result.
4. **`--count N`.** Produce N videos (the default demo run, or N of a given
   `--scenario`).
5. **Single-session batch.** Reuse one Vite server and one Chromium browser
   across the batch, with a fresh page/context per item so a failed clip cannot
   poison the next.
6. **Output naming.** Deterministic, collision-free default names per item;
   document how `--output` behaves for batches (directory or prefix).
7. **Summary + exit code.** Final summary (path, outcome, complete/capHit,
   bytes per item); exit non-zero if any item failed or hit the cap.
8. **Backwards compatibility.** A single `--scenario` invocation behaves exactly
   as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (list):** `npm run capture -- --list-scenarios` lists every implemented
  scenario (value + one-line effect) from the shared registry, exits 0, and
  boots no browser or server; `--json` emits a machine-readable array.
- **AC2 (all):** `npm run capture -- --all-scenarios` produces one video per
  registered scenario in a single invocation and reports success/failure per
  item.
- **AC3 (count):** `npm run capture -- --count N` produces exactly N videos
  (N >= 1); with `--scenario S` all N use S, otherwise the default demo run;
  `--count 0`, missing or non-numeric values error clearly.
- **AC4 (single session):** across a batch the Vite server and Chromium browser
  start exactly once (asserted via instrumentation/count), with a fresh
  page/context per item.
- **AC5 (naming):** items get deterministic, collision-free default output
  paths; an existing file is never silently overwritten by a different item.
- **AC6 (summary/exit):** a batch prints a final aggregate summary and exits
  non-zero if any item failed or hit the cap; a single-item failure does not
  abort the remaining items.
- **AC7 (tests):** hermetic unit tests cover arg parsing (`--list-scenarios`,
  `--all-scenarios`, `--count`, combinations and invalid input), the registry
  contents, output-name generation, and batch result/exit-code aggregation
  (no browser); existing capture tests continue to pass.
- **AC8 (docs):** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the `README.md` capture
  section document the list/all/count flags with examples; `--help` updated.
- **AC9 (suite):** `npm test`, `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Constraints

- Capture stays outside the shipped bundle; the shared registry must be
  browser-free and consumed by dev-gated code only.
- The browser/encode path cannot run under vitest (the canvas is stubbed), so
  all new decision logic (registry, naming, aggregation) must be pure and
  unit-tested; the browser path is exercised by `npm run capture`.
- Serial-by-default batched execution (one browser) to avoid host resource
  contention.
- Existing single-scenario, `--duration` and `--scripted` behaviour unchanged.

## Risks, assumptions and failure modes

- **Assumption:** the three registered scenarios (`boss`, `boss-four-hits`,
  `defeat`) stay the complete set. Because the registry becomes the single
  source, a future scenario added in `src/core/devScenario.ts` without
  registering it would drift from the CLI. Mitigation: make the game resolver
  consume the registry and add a registry <-> resolver test.
- **Failure mode:** a per-item browser/encode failure must not poison the
  shared session (one Vite server + one Chromium browser). Mitigation: a fresh
  page/context per item, per-item error capture, and continue to the next item
  (AC6).
- **Failure mode:** deterministic default batch names could collide on a
  re-run, or an existing file could be silently overwritten by a different
  item. Mitigation: item-scoped, collision-free names plus a never-silently-
  overwrite check (AC5).
- **Failure mode:** a batch item that never signals a run-end could hang.
  Mitigation: the existing per-item `--max-duration` cap bounds each item and
  the summary reports `capHit` per item (AC6).
- **Risk (host resources):** parallel capture would exhaust CPU/GPU on the dev
  host, so execution stays serial by default (one browser; see Constraints).
- **Assumption:** `--list-scenarios` must not boot Vite/Chromium, so the
  registry has to be importable by bare Node — a browser-free `.mjs` module
  following the `capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` precedent.
- **Scope-creep risk:** ad-hoc extras (a `--filter` flag, per-scenario duration
  overrides, an HTML index page) are out of scope; record each as a
  `discovered-from` work item rather than widening this change.

## OPEN QUESTIONs (non-blocking, recommended defaults)

- Should `--all-scenarios` include the default no-scenario demo run?
  *Recommended:* NO (an explicit `--include-demo` opt-in), because the demo is
  non-deterministic and multi-minute.
- `--output` in a batch: treat it as a directory (*recommended*) or a filename
  prefix?
- Should `--count` combine with `--all-scenarios` (N repeats of every scenario)?
  *Recommended:* reject the combination, or define it explicitly as N x all.
  Directed to the producer at plan/implement time.

## Key files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — flags, batch orchestration, summary/exit
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.d.mts` — types for new exports
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (+ `.d.mts`) — shared browser-free scenario
  registry (or extend `capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`)
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — consume the shared registry
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — hermetic tests
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `README.md` — documentation

## Related work

- **Create full video playthroughs** (AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU) — `discovered-from`;
  added the full-run capture and the `defeat` scenario this builds on.
- **Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic ...** (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ) —
  `related-to`; the capture epic.
- **Spike: automated gameplay video capture** (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK) — the
  pipeline this extends.

## Appendix: clarification

- The operator asked (this session) whether scenarios can be listed, all
  generated in one call, and N videos generated; none of the three exists today.
  This work item adds them. Approval to write code has NOT been given
  (create-only).
- Q (intake evaluation, this session, Map): "Is the work item defined well
  enough to skip the interactive interview?" — Answer (agent, Map): "Yes. The
  brief already carries a problem statement, user stories, 9 measurable ACs,
  constraints, key files and related work; an interactive interview would only
  repeat information already recorded in the work item." Source: `wl show
  AH-0MUZM8ATZ002AKFP --json`; repo inspection of
  `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`, `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`,
  `src/core/devScenario.ts`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `README.md`.
- OPEN QUESTION (retained for plan/implement; non-blocking, no answer supplied
  this session): demo inclusion in `--all-scenarios` (preferred **NO**;
  `--include-demo` opt-in), `--output` batch semantics (preferred a
  **directory**), and `--count` combined with `--all-scenarios` (preferred
  **reject**, or define as N x all). The recommended defaults are advisory; the
  producer's choice at plan time wins.
- Related-work research (find-related, this session): appended the automated
  report below (`AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN`, `AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123`,
  `AH-0MTFSM3IR001QR0C` plus three repo file matches); the manual **Related
  work** section above remains authoritative.

- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (completed)

# Report script counts soft-deleted children

**discovered-from:AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2**

## Problem

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) shows an incorrect **Children** count when a parent has soft-deleted children.

- `wl delete <id>` is a **soft delete** — it sets `status=deleted` and `deletedBy`, and the item remains visible via `wl show <parent> --children`.
- `wl list --parent <id>` correctly **excludes** deleted items.
- `render_report.py` (`render_from_wl`) counts `len(data["children"])` from `wl show --children`, so it **includes** the tombstones.

Observed on AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2: 7 active children + 6 soft-deleted coverage-gap children reported as `Children: 13`; `wl list --parent` correctly reports 7.

## Expected behaviour

The report's child count matches the active child set — i.e. it excludes items with `status=deleted` (or `deletedBy` set). Ideally the shared `wl show --children` behaviour and the report agree with `wl list --parent`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a parent with children.
2. `wl delete <one-child> --json` (soft delete).
3. Run `python3 skill/report/scripts/render_report.py <parent-id> --skill-name plan ...`.
4. Observe the **Children** count includes the deleted child.

## Suggested fix

Filter deleted children in `render_from_wl` before counting (e.g. `[c for c in children if c.get("status") != "deleted" and not c.get("deletedBy")]`), or make `wl show --children` exclude deleted items consistently with `wl list --parent`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The report's **Children** count excludes soft-deleted items.
- A test covers a parent with a mix of active and soft-deleted children.
- Behaviour is consistent with `wl list --parent`.

# Hull Full overlay: metronomic fire sounds + restart countdown (AH-0MV0QPO4N009KWVT)

**Headline:** When the hold-full power-up choice overlay opens, the player's
active weapon-fire cues keep pulsing on the exact 80 BPM beat grid at a reduced
volume (no bullets, no simulation) and, once the player picks an option, a
3-2-1 countdown lands one count per beat before gameplay restarts.

## Problem statement

Opening the hold-full choice (`MineralChoiceScene`) pauses `PlayScene` at the
SceneManager level, which freezes the shared beat clock and stops all fire
audio. The abrupt silence breaks the run's rhythmic feel. The pause should
instead feel like a held-down groove: the ship's firing *sounds* keep ticking on
the same beat (quieter, with no projectiles), and the player's selection is
followed by a beat-locked 3-2-1 countdown that restarts play on the next beat.

## Users

- **Player (game):** wants a less jarring interruption — the rhythm they were
  playing to continues through the power-up choice and restarts cleanly.
- **Player (demo/attract mode viewer):** the attract-mode run should keep its
  audible cadence and resume after the bot's auto-select through the same
  countdown.

Example user stories:

- *As a player*, when the hold fills and the power-up choice appears, I still
  hear the ship firing on the beat (quieter, no bullets) so the game doesn't
  feel frozen.
- *As a player*, after I choose an upgrade I get a beat-locked "3, 2, 1" and
  the ship starts firing again exactly on the next beat.

## Existing state

- The hold-full overlay is `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`, launched as a
  modal above the launcher (GDD §4.5). `PlayScene.openMineralChoice()` calls
  `setPaused(true)` then `this.scene.pause()`; the gym launcher
  (`GymFormationScene.openMineralChoice()`) launches the overlay and pauses its
  scene (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:1276`).
- Player auto-fire is globally quantised to a **silent 80 BPM beat grid**
  (`src/utils/beat.ts`), with per-weapon subdivisions — Cannon 2/beat
  (375 ms), Spread/Dual 1/beat (750 ms), Rapid 6/beat (125 ms) — and every
  active weapon phase-locked to the same grid (`Player.tryFire`,
  `Player.getFireInterval`, `Player.getActiveWeapons`).
- Fire cues are played per firing weapon via
  `PlayScene._playShootCue(weaponId)` → `onWeaponFired` in the shared combat
  core (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:557`). Each cue is a baked ToneForge
  asset routed through `src/audio/effects.ts` and `src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts`,
  which already supports a per-play `volume` option (`SfxPlayOptions.volume`).
- Pausing the scene stops both the beat clock and the fire cues, so the overlay
  is currently silent.

## Desired change

- On holding-full overlay open, continue the **player's** fire cues on the same
  beat grid at a reduced volume (**0.3× normal**, one tunable constant) for
  **all currently active player weapons** (cannon + every collected timed
  weapon), with no projectiles spawned and no gameplay simulation advanced.
  **No enemy cues** play (gameplay is stopped).
- The rhythm is **continuous and phase-locked**: the ghost ticks during the
  overlay, the countdown counts, and the first real shots after resume all sit
  on the same beat grid (the beat timeline does not restart or jump).
- When the player selects an option, a **3-2-1 countdown** plays with **one
  count per beat** (750 ms at the default 80 BPM): each count shows large
  on-screen text ("3", "2", "1") on the overlay and plays a **distinct
  countdown audio cue**. The reduced-volume fire rhythm **continues underneath
  the countdown** (producer decision).
- After the "1" beat, gameplay resumes on the next beat and the ship's real
  fire continues on the same grid.
- Implemented once in the shared overlay/launcher seam so the game and every
  gym that launches `MineralChoiceScene` behave identically (AGENTS.md gym↔game
  parity).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Reduced-volume metronomic fire while paused:** When the hold-full
  overlay opens, every currently active player weapon's fire cue plays on that
  weapon's exact beat-grid cadence at **0.3× normal volume** (single named
  tunable constant, e.g. `HOLD_FULL_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`). No projectiles are
  spawned and no gameplay simulation advances while the overlay is open.
- [ ] **AC2 — Active player weapons only:** the metronomic cues cover the
  cannon and every collected timed weapon (`Player.getActiveWeapons()`), and no
  enemy cue (or other gameplay cue) plays during the overlay.
- [ ] **AC3 — Rhythm continuity / phase-lock:** the first ghost tick after the
  overlay opens lands on the beat tick the next real shot would have used
  (phase preserved) and the cadence continues on the grid; the same grid is
  continuous through the countdown into resumed live fire (no phase jump or
  restart). Verified by asserting tick times against `src/utils/beat.ts` grid
  maths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Beat-locked 3-2-1 countdown on selection:** when a selection is
  made, gameplay stays paused and a 3-2-1 countdown plays, one count per beat
  (750 ms at the default 80 BPM) on the beat grid, each count showing on-screen
  text and playing a distinct countdown audio cue; the reduced-volume fire
  rhythm continues underneath. Gameplay resumes on the beat immediately after
  "1" (three beats after selection).
- [ ] **AC5 — Shared overlay / gym↔game parity:** the behaviour is implemented
  in the shared overlay/launcher seam and runs identically in `PlayScene` and
  every gym that launches `MineralChoiceScene`; no duplicated divergent logic
  (verified by the gym↔game equivalence suite).
- [ ] **AC6 — Demo/attract mode:** the existing demo auto-select still drives
  the same selection → countdown → resume path (no stall, no divergence).
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing and full suite:** automated unit and scene-level tests
  cover the metronomic scheduling (with a recording SFX provider and a fake
  clock), the reduced volume, the countdown timing/on-beat counts, the
  continuous-grid guarantee, and gym↔game parity; `npm run typecheck`, the full
  project test suite and the build all pass.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including code comments, the GDD (§4.5 hold-full choice / §7.3
  audio) and the README, plus `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` if a new
  cue is added.

## Constraints

- **Volume:** reduced volume is a fixed ratio of normal, default **0.3×**,
  expressed as one named tunable constant (not scattered magic numbers).
- **Countdown audio:** prefer a short synthesised **tone** cue; use a
  **public-domain voice countdown** only if a suitable, licence-cleared voice
  asset can be sourced (producer decision). If a new cue is needed it must
  follow the existing ToneForge baked-asset pipeline (recipe + manifest +
  checksum + cue-mapping doc).
- **Audio plumbing:** reuse the existing shared `AudioContext`/provider
  (`src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts`) and its per-play `volume` option; do not create a
  second AudioContext, and do not silence/enable other SFX globally.
- **No music:** GDD §7.3 keeps background music out of MVP scope; the countdown
  is an SFX cue only.
- **No bullets / no simulation:** the overlay continuation is audio + on-screen
  text only; gameplay entities must remain frozen.
- **Determinism:** scheduling must derive from the beat clock/grid maths, not
  wall-clock reads inside gameplay code, so it stays testable and consistent
  with the existing beat-accent design.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — run the reduced-volume metronomic fire,
  render the on-screen "3/2/1" countdown, and defer resume until the countdown
  completes.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass the active-weapon fire schedule + reduced
  volume into the overlay; advance/re-base the beat clock across the pause and
  resume on the beat after "1".
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — same launch payload/resume
  behaviour for gym parity.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — per-play volume on the player fire cues (e.g. a
  shared `playWeaponFireSound(weaponId, options?)` helper) and a new
  `playCountdownTickSound()` if a dedicated cue is added.
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts`, `audio/toneforge/recipes/` and
  `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new countdown cue wiring (only if a new cue
  is added).
- `src/utils/beat.ts` — reused grid maths (no change expected).
- `src/core/rules.ts` or a small shared module — the reduced-volume constant and
  countdown length (beats) as named tunables.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — overlay text styling/timing constants if needed.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`,
  `src/audio/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` and the gym↔game equivalence suite —
  new/extended coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`,
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — documentation.

## Related work

- **Hold-full choice overlay (AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q)** — the overlay and its
  single `onSelect` contract this change extends.
- **Beat-aligned fire grid (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B)** — the 80 BPM grid and
  `src/utils/beat.ts` this feature reuses.
- **Demo bot auto-select of hold-full (AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB)** — demo mode must
  route through the same countdown path.
- **Beat-synced explosion accents (AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3)** — the existing shared
  audio-scheduling seam (`setExplosionBeatClock`) and the pattern for
  quantised, testable cue scheduling.
- **Switch game audio to ToneForge (AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J)** — the baked-asset
  pipeline a new countdown cue would follow.
- **Power-up collect pop cue (AH-0MUBYSNGU0051XVO)** — example of a small,
  self-contained new SFX cue with a unit test.
- **Seed intent discovery:** the requested behaviour was supplied directly by
  the producer; no prior work item existed for it.
- **Automated find-related sweep (marginal):** AH-0MUQOY9PD004SL87 (docs
  updates), AH-0MUD9ZNBK005WKLY (leaderboard module test) and AH-0MUBYSNGU0051XVO
  (power-up collect pop cue) — only the last is directly relevant (a small
  self-contained SFX cue precedent); the others matched on generic keywords.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — phase continuity across a paused scene.** The game beat clock is
  frozen while paused, so the overlay must drive its own (wall-clock) ticks and
  the beat timeline must be re-based on resume. Mitigation: derive all ticks
  from `src/utils/beat.ts` grid maths and assert grid membership in tests;
  decide in implementation whether to advance the shared clock during the
  overlay or re-base on resume — either way AC3 pins the observable outcome.
- **Risk — audio scheduling jitter.** Phaser scene timers are frame-quantised;
  ghost ticks may sit a few ms off the exact grid. Mitigation: AC3 asserts
  *phase/grid membership of scheduled times*, not sub-frame audio latency, and
  tests use a fake clock.
- **Risk — mix clash.** Countdown tones plus continued fire could clip.
  Mitigation: reduced 0.3× fire volume plus a short countdown cue; keep the
  countdown cue distinct and modest.
- **Risk — scope creep (new audio asset pipeline).** Adding a baked cue touches
  ToneForge recipes, manifest, checksums and docs. Mitigation: prefer reusing an
  existing short tick cue or a runtime-safe tone; add a new baked cue only if a
  suitable existing cue is unavailable. Any additional opportunity (e.g. a
  voice countdown pack) is recorded as a separate linked work item, not folded
  into this one.
- **Risk — gym parity drift.** The overlay is shared, but the launch payload
  lives in each launcher. Mitigation: AC5 requires parity coverage via the
  equivalence suite.
- **Assumption — reward application timing.** The chosen power-up is applied
  when the countdown completes (gameplay "restart"), not at the instant of the
  click; this keeps the single `onSelect` contract as the resume trigger.
  *Rationale:* avoids adding a second callback and matches "restart countdown".
- **Assumption — countdown length.** Three counts, one per beat, with resume on
  the following beat (≈2.25 s at 80 BPM). *Rationale:* the seed intent explicitly
  says 3-2-1.
- **Assumption — ghost fire stops with play.** The metronomic reduced-volume
  fire ends when live gameplay resumes (it is a placeholder for real fire, which
  takes over on the same grid). *Rationale:* producer chose to continue it
  *through* the countdown but it is not required after resume.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which fire sound(s) should continue as the metronomic overlay?" —
  Answer (producer): **B** — all currently active player weapon sounds, no enemy
  weapon sounds. Source: interactive reply (2026-10-09).
- Q: "What should the reduced volume be?" — Answer (producer): **A** — a fixed
  ratio of normal volume. Follow-up confirmed the value **0.3×** normal.
  Source: interactive replies (2026-10-09). Prior answer: "fixed ratio
  (unspecified)"; final accepted answer: 0.3×.
- Q: "How should the 3-2-1 countdown be presented?" — Answer (producer): **C** —
  both on-screen text and a distinct audio cue per count; use a tone in place of
  voice unless a suitable public-domain voice countdown can be found. Source:
  interactive reply (2026-10-09).
- Q: "Does the metronomic reduced-volume fire continue during the countdown or
  stop when the countdown starts?" — Answer (producer): **B** — it continues
  underneath the countdown until gameplay resumes. Source: interactive reply
  (2026-10-09).

_Reviews:_ Completeness — added the automated find-related list; Capture
fidelity — consolidated the duplicate volume Q/A into one entry with the
prior/final answers; Related-work & traceability — referenced the find-related
sweep and confirmed doc/cue-mapping links; Risks & assumptions — added the
phase-continuity and audio-pipeline scope-creep mitigations and the reward-
timing/ghost-fire-cutoff assumptions; Polish & handoff — tightened wording and
AC phrasing.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-12 — Plan skill: decomposed into 8 child work items (test seams →
  metronomic fire → countdown cue → countdown/resume → gym↔game parity →
  demo/attract → full-suite verification → documentation). Dependencies wired
  with `wl dep add`; AC coverage review **proceed** (100%); six review stages
  completed. No producer approval required (effort Medium, risk High).

The demo/competent bot's steering and forward model use hard-coded thruster constants instead of the ship's configured values, so it does not automatically adjust when thruster configuration changes.

Evidence:
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` hard-codes `frictionDeceleration: 100`, `playerSpeed: 175`, `assumedBulletSpeed: 200`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` `mayThrust()` computes stopping distance from `frictionDeceleration` (a tunable), not the ship's configured `friction`/deceleration.

- Reverse thrust (acceleration/max speed/enabled) is not represented in the bot's model at all.

Goal: feed the live ShipConfig (forward thrust acceleration, max speed, friction/deceleration, and reverse acceleration/max speed/enabled) through the bot's snapshot/context into the steering + forward-model estimates, so any change to the player's thruster configuration is picked up automatically by the bot. Update tunables to be defaults/overrides rather than authoritative values. Full test suite and docs updated.

Medium priority: not blocking the bot's ability to use reverse (AH-0MV1J0OHP0072XA5), but required for correctness under custom thruster tuning.

# Intake Brief — Add 5 new levels before the boss showcasing the classic-arcade enemy roster

**Work item:** AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2 (feature, high)
**Headline:** Grow the campaign from 5 to 10 regular levels (plus the boss) so the
eight classic-arcade enemies added this sprint are showcased in curated, varied
encounters, with every player-targeting archetype paired alongside other kinds
of enemies.

## Problem statement

This sprint delivered eight classic-arcade enemy archetypes (Space Invaders
`march`, Galaga `capturer`, Pac-Man ghosts, Centipede, Robotron `grunt` horde,
Defender `raider`, Missile Command `orbital-strike`, Frogger `lane-traffic`),
but the shipped campaign is still only five levels: Levels 1–3 formation drift
(no fire), Level 4 enemy fire, Level 5 orbital Phasers. The new roster is only
reachable in the gym scenes — a player completing a normal run never sees it.

The operator wants **five more levels before the boss** to show the new enemies
off, and because some of the new enemies specifically target the player, those
archetypes must appear **alongside other kinds of enemies** rather than in
isolation.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, I want the run to keep escalating with genuinely
  new enemy movement and attack styles, so the campaign does not feel like the
  same five levels with more bullets."
- **Designer/content author** — "As a designer, I want a deterministic,
  data-driven way to place a specific new archetype in a specific wave pairing,
  while still letting some waves vary between runs."
- **Engineer** — "As an engineer, I want the campaign to grow through the
  existing `LEVELS` skeleton + difficulty-curve config, with gym↔game parity,
  so the change is testable and adds no divergent code paths."

## Existing state

- `src/waves/Formations.ts` defines `LEVELS` (5 static levels) and
  `LEVEL_COUNT = LEVELS.length`; the boss (`BOSS_ENEMY_KEY = 'boss'`) is
  triggered after the final level clears.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` + `src/core/configStore.ts`
  (`defaultDifficultyCurves`) provide the per-wave generation layer
  (`curve` / `fixed` / `dynamic`); `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` merges it over
  the static skeleton and appends configured levels beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`.
- `WaveManager.levelCount` / `isFinalLevel` derive from `levels.length`, so
  HUD `Level N of 5` and the boss trigger adapt automatically once more levels
  exist (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` reads them).
- Spawner-gated archetypes are wave opt-in flags: `ghosts`, `centipede`,
  `horde`, `laneTraffic`; `march`, `capturer`, `raider`, `orbital-strike`,
  `lane-traffic` are CSV-backed rows. `defaultCandidatePool()` (the `dynamic`
  source) excludes `harvester`, `asteroid` and `grunt` (spawner-delivered).
- `HARVESTER_MIN_LEVEL = 4`, `HARVESTER_MAX_LEVEL = 5` — the Harvester only
  spawns in the two hardest regular levels and must be re-ranged for 10 levels.

## Desired change

Grow the campaign to **10 regular levels + the boss**, keeping Levels 1–3 as
the no-fire onboarding section and introducing/interleaving the classic-arcade
roster from Level 4 onward. The organising principle is **variety of movement
and attack styles between adjacent levels**, and **every wave that includes a
player-targeting archetype also contains at least one non-player-targeting
kind**.

Proposed ordering (open to refinement during implementation, but the
style-variety and pairing invariants are the requirement):

| Lvl | Name | Movement style | Attack style | Classic showcase / pairing |
|-----|------|----------------|--------------|-----------------------------|
| 1 | Entry | V-formation drift | none (no fire) | existing onboarding |
| 2 | Descent | Diver/swarm drift | none (no fire) | existing onboarding |
| 3 | The Core | Rect + V pairs | none (no fire) | existing onboarding |
| 4 | Firestorm | Mixed drift | aimed/spread/radial | existing fire introduction |
| 5 | Predictable Death | Fixed orbital paths | radial (memorisable) | existing Phaser |
| 6 | Invasion | **Stepping march** | aimed + tractor pull | `march` + `capturer` (targeter) |
| 7 | Segmented Assault | **Winding chain + pursuit** | radial + none | `centipede` + ghosts (targeter) |
| 8 | Gridlock | **Lanes + homing + patrol/dive** | none + aimed | `lane-traffic` + `grunt` (targeter) + `raider` (targeter) |
| 9 | Orbital Siege | **Telegraphed arcs + orbitals + pursuit** | detonation burst + radial | `orbital-strike` + `phaser` + ghosts (targeter) |
| 10 | The Gauntlet | **Dense mixed finale** | full mix | all remaining roster; every wave mixes targeters with non-targeters |

**Player-targeting archetypes** (assumption, to confirm in review):
`capturer` (tractor-beam pull), `ghost-chase/ambush/flank` (steering pursuit),
`grunt` (homing horde), `raider` (committed dive). Non-targeting kinds provide
the required counterweight in every such wave.

**Authoring mode (mixture of static + dynamic):** each new archetype's
debut/featured wave is authored as a static `fixed` wave (guaranteeing the
showcase), while the remaining waves in Levels 6–10 may be `dynamic` (seeded
per-run regeneration from their curve) so repeat runs vary. Static `fixed`
waves with no counterpart fall back to `curve` safely (existing behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Campaign size** — The campaign defines exactly **10 regular levels plus
   the boss**; `WaveManager.levelCount === 10`, the boss triggers only after the
   final wave of Level 10 clears, and the HUD renders `Level N of 10`.
2. **Roster coverage** — Every one of the eight sprint archetypes
   (`march`, `capturer`, `ghost-*`, `centipede`, `grunt`, `raider`,
   `orbital-strike`, `lane-traffic`) appears at least once in the campaign,
   verified by an automated test over the merged campaign.
3. **Player-targeter pairing** — Every wave containing a player-targeting
   archetype (`capturer`, `ghost-*`, `grunt`, `raider`) also contains at least
   one non-player-targeting kind; enforced by an automated invariant test.
4. **Style variety** — Adjacent levels differ in dominant movement/attack
   style; the mapping is documented and an automated test asserts no two
   adjacent levels share the same style profile.
5. **Onboarding preserved & authoring mix** — Levels 1–3 remain
   `shootEnabled: false` and Levels 4–10 fire; the campaign uses **both**
   `fixed` and `dynamic` waves, with every featured showcase wave `fixed` so the
   new archetype is guaranteed present for a given run seed.
6. **Difficulty continuity** — The 10-level difficulty curve is non-decreasing
   and Level 10's final target exceeds the previous campaign's final target;
   the Harvester level range is extended to the new hardest levels.
7. **Gym↔game parity & quality** — New waves reuse the shared spawners/entities
   and honour the repo-wide duplicate-body guard; all existing gym scenes still
   pass; full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related
   documentation (GDD, README, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
   `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`) is updated. (CHANGELOG excluded — managed
   by the ship release pipeline.)

## Constraints

- No divergent copies: gameplay must run the same code in gyms and the game
  (repo-wide duplicate-body guard in `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`).
- Levels 1–3 must stay no-fire (GDD §2.4); `FIRST_FIRING_LEVEL = 4`.
- `dynamic` waves may only draw archetypes the runtime auto-sequencer supports
  as wave groups; spawner-gated archetypes (`ghosts`, `centipede`, `horde`,
  `laneTraffic`) must be delivered via their per-wave opt-in flags on `fixed`
  waves. Featured archetypes must remain present regardless of seed.
- No unplayable campaign or crash on any fallback path
  (`sequencedLevels` safety contract).
- UK English in all written output.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — extend `LEVELS` to 10 level definitions with the
  new waves/opt-in flags; update the module doc-comment mapping.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — add rows for Levels 6–10 and mark featured
  waves `fixed`, chosen waves `dynamic`.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — extend `defaultDifficultyCurves()` /
  `DEFAULT_FIXED_LEVELS` / `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` for Levels 6–10.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — verify no changes needed (append/merge path);
  add coverage if new curation is required.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — doc-comment updates ("Level 5" → final level);
  verify boss trigger via `isFinalLevel`.
- `src/waves/HarvesterSpawner.ts` — extend `HARVESTER_MAX_LEVEL` to the new
  hardest levels.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — HUD label comment/`of 10`; verify boss entry.
- `src/waves/Formations.test.ts`, `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`,
  `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`
  — update level-count/level-number assertions; add coverage and diversity tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` —
  document the 10-level campaign and the pairing/variety rules.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** player-targeting archetypes are `capturer`, `ghost-*`,
  `grunt`, `raider`. Mitigation: confirm in review; the pairing invariant is
  parameterised by this set so it is easy to extend.
- **Risk — existing-test churn:** several tests hard-code `LEVEL_COUNT === 5`,
  "Level 5 fewer enemies" and Level 4 ≤ Level 5. Mitigation: update them as part
  of the change and keep the difficulty ramp assertions meaningful.
- **Risk — spawner-gated archetypes cannot be `dynamic` candidates.**
  Mitigation: deliver them on `fixed` waves via the existing opt-in flags.
- **Risk — difficulty spike / boss reached overpowered.** Mitigation: keep the
  curve non-decreasing and tune `targetDifficulty` for Levels 6–10.
- **Risk — scope creep** into power-up/weapon roster work
  (AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4). Mitigation: record as separate linked work, not in
  scope here.
- **Risk — endogenous hazards and wave completion:** `lane-traffic` and
  `orbital-strike` are non-blocking hazards and must not gate wave clear
  (existing accounting contract).

## Related work

- New enemies from classic arcade games — **AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52** (completed,
  parent of the eight archetype deliveries below).
- Documentation integration for the classic arcade roster —
  **AH-0MV01ER86000DNRF** (completed).
- Research catalogue and engine-constraint validation —
  **AH-0MV01EBUR003BDNK** (completed) → `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`.
- Per-archetype deliveries: `march` AH-0MV01EDZS0005R20, `capturer`
  AH-0MV01EFII008298D, ghosts AH-0MV01EH2U008XT3Q, centipede
  AH-0MV01EJ92008ZZ86, grunt AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6, raider AH-0MV01EM7U0033W7L,
  orbital-strike AH-0MV01ENX00055CG1, lane-traffic AH-0MV01EPM40008N8T.
- Per-wave generation modes (curve/fixed/dynamic) — **AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT**.
- Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign —
  **AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD**.
- Implement WaveManager — wave and level progression —
  **AH-0MU72ZK3P006CH9G**.
- Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5' — **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2**.
- Difficulty-curve config, codec and CSV loader — **AH-0MUITRZZE000OYQE**.
- Docs: `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`
  (§3.2, §4.1, §2.4–2.5).
- Harvester documentation updates — **AH-0MUJRW0U6007PMB2** (completed);
  relevant because `HARVESTER_MAX_LEVEL` must be re-ranged for the longer
  campaign.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MUJRW0U6007PMB2** – Harvester documentation updates (completed).
- Repository file matches: `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- Full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — Campaign placement: append (a), replace/re-number (b), or separate mode
  (c)? — **Answer (operator): (b)** "the key is variety of movement and attack
  styles between levels". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 — Authoring mode: static `fixed` (a), `curve` (b), `dynamic` (c)? —
  **Answer (operator): a mixture of (a) and (c)** — hand-authored static waves
  plus seeded `dynamic` regeneration. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 — Player-targeter pairing/progression: progressive showcase (a), dense
  from the start (b), one archetype per level (c)? — **Answer (operator): (a)**
  progressive showcase with targeters paired with other kinds. Source:
  interactive reply.
- Q4 — Total campaign length after interleaving? — **Answer (operator): (a)**
  10 levels + boss; ordering is the agent's responsibility and existing levels
  may be redesigned. Source: interactive reply.
- Q5 — No-fire onboarding: keep Levels 1–3 no-fire and interleave showcase from
  Level 4 (a), add non-firing targeters early (b), drop onboarding (c)? —
  **Answer (operator): (a)**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q6 (assumption, not asked) — Player-targeting set is `capturer`, `ghost-*`,
  `grunt`, `raider`. Evidence: `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` §3 (ghosts
  steer at the live player), §5 (grunts homing-steer), §6 (raiders dive at the
  player), §2 (capturers pull the player). OPEN QUESTION for review if the set
  should differ.

# Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** AH-0MV29NWI1007NKN7

## Problem statement

The enemy classification system (movement/attack classes added to
`src/data/enemy-configs.csv` by **Enemy classification system for balanced wave
design** (AH-0MV29NWI1007NKN7)) is descriptive and validated, but nothing in the
game or tooling consumes it yet. This follow-up makes the classification
*actionable*: the wave sequencer and/or balance checks use it to compose and
verify balanced waves.

## User story

As a wave designer, I want the runtime wave generator to respect enemy
classification rules (for example: opening waves contain only formation/melee
archetypes; no wave is composed entirely of chasers; a wave has a bounded mix of
ranged attackers), so that generated waves are balanced without manual review.

## Scope (to be refined at intake)

- Consume `movementClass` / `attackClass` in the candidate pool and sequencer
  (`src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`) or a new
  balance-validation layer.
- Add explicit, testable balance rules (composition constraints / quotas).
- Keep gym↔game parity: any rule enforced in the game must be observable in the
  relevant gym/dev-utility scene.
- Documentation updates in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by **Enemy classification system for balanced wave design**
  (AH-0MV29NWI1007NKN7) — the classification field must exist first.

## Acceptance criteria (provisional)

1. At least one balance rule based on the classification is enforced by the wave
   generator / validation layer, with unit tests.
2. Rules are deterministic and seeded, preserving reproducible runs.
3. Documentation describes the rules and how to tune them.
4. Full project test suite passes.

# Upgrade and weapon descriptions

## Problem statement

When the mineral hold fills, the modal choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`) lists each option as a name plus at most one detail line: the "what improves" change summary for owned level-ups, or a `★ New` badge for an unowned item. It never says **what the item actually does**. A player offered an unfamiliar `Arc`, or `Spread Shot Lv.4`, cannot tell what the weapon/power-up does before committing the pick. Add one short, player-facing description sentence to every option so the choice is self-explanatory.

## Users

- **Player (informed choice):** "As a player, when the hold fills and I'm offered an upgrade, I want a one-line sentence telling me what the weapon or power-up does, so I can choose sensibly even if I haven't seen it before."
- **Player (new vs upgrade):** "As a player, I want a new item to show what it does alongside its `★ New` badge, not just the badge."
- **Designer/tuner:** "As a designer, I want the sentence to come from the shared catalogue so the overlay copy, the gym help copy and the implemented behaviour can never drift apart."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Description on every option.** `ChoiceOption` (`src/powerups/choice.ts`) gains an optional `description` field populated for **all four** option kinds — `weapon`, `powerup`, `weapon-level`, `power-up-level` (producer Q3 = A). Existing fields (`name`, `changeSummary`, `isNew`, `level`, `kind`) are unchanged; the field is optional so existing `ChoiceStrategy` implementations and tests keep compiling.
- **AC2 — Rendering.** `MineralChoiceScene` renders the description as its **own line** beneath the option name, with the existing change-summary / `★ New` line beneath that — a three-line block per option (producer Q2 = A). Option labels (`"1.  Spread Shot Lv.3"`) are unchanged, and a dedicated getter (e.g. `getDescriptionLines()`) exposes the rendered descriptions for tests; the existing `getDetailLines()` contract (summary / `★ New`) is unchanged.
- **AC3 — Level-neutral wording.** The reused catalogue descriptions are rewritten so each sentence is accurate for **both** a temporary field pickup **and** a permanent hold-full reward (producer Q1 = B): hard-coded temporary-duration clauses (e.g. "for 10 s", "for 8 s") that would mislead on a permanent pick are removed or made level-neutral, while the concrete per-level deltas stay in the existing `changeSummary`. Every description remains non-empty.
- **AC4 — Single source of truth.** The description is resolved from the shared catalogues (`WEAPON_CATALOGUE` / `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`, via the shared `getHelpEntry` resolver in `src/utils/gymHelp.ts` or an exported equivalent); no description text is duplicated in the scene or the choice layer, so the overlay and the gym help show identical copy.
- **AC5 — Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every gym that opens the hold-full choice, because they share `MineralChoiceScene` and `powerups/choice`; no divergent copy or second render path is introduced (AGENTS.md parity convention).
- **AC6 — Testing/validation.** Unit and scene tests cover: `description` populated for all four option kinds; the shared-resolution (no duplication) contract; the three-line overlay rendering plus the existing summary / `★ New` line; the no-description fallback (no empty line); and the level-neutral catalogue wording guard. Coverage serves a meaningful purpose (TDD preferred).
- **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the README, and Game Design Document §4.4.1 / §4.5 (the "each option additionally shows" list gains the description line).
- **AC8 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour lives once (`src/powerups/choice.ts`, `src/utils/gymHelp.ts`, `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`) and is consumed by the game and every gym.
- **Backward compatibility:** extend `ChoiceOption` with an **optional** field only; the pluggable `ChoiceStrategy` contract is unchanged.
- **Do not break existing assertions:** `MineralChoiceScene.getOptionLabels()` and `getDetailLines()` are asserted in tests — the description is a separate game object/getter.
- **Preserve docs-test invariants:** `src/utils/gymHelp.test.ts` asserts every catalogue description is non-empty and the AOE descriptions match `/AOE/i`; `src/scenes/HelpScene.test.ts` renders `entry.description`. Rewrites must keep descriptions non-empty and the AOE wording intact.
- **No duplicated copy:** reuse the shared catalogue resolver; never inline description strings in the scene/choice layer.
- **Run-scoped:** no leaderboard impact.
- **Scope boundary:** the existing change-summary computation and the 3-offer mechanism are unchanged; this item is presentation + catalogue wording only.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `ChoiceOption` carries `id`, `name`, `kind`, `level?`, `changeSummary?`, `isNew?`. `buildChoiceCandidates` populates `changeSummary` for `weapon-level`/`power-up-level` and `isNew` for unowned base entries. There is **no** description field.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — labels at `y = 210 + index * 64`; one detail line at `y + 28` = `changeSummary`, else `★ New`. `getDetailLines()` returns those.
- `src/utils/gymHelp.ts` — `getHelpEntry(id)` resolves `{ name, description, drawIcon }` from `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` / `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` / `RESET_DROP`; the gym help overlay is its only current consumer.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` / `src/powerups/types.ts` — catalogue `description` fields exist for every choice item and are the shared player-facing copy; several still assert a temporary duration (e.g. "for 10 s").

## Desired change

Every hold-full option shows three lines — the option name, a one-line description of what the weapon/power-up does, then the existing change-summary or `★ New` line — with the description text resolved from the shared catalogue and the catalogue wording made level-neutral so it reads correctly for both a timed pickup and a permanent reward.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — Add `description?: string` to `ChoiceOption`; populate it in `toChoiceOption`/`buildChoiceCandidates` for all four option kinds.
- `src/utils/gymHelp.ts` — Expose/reuse the shared id → description resolver so the overlay and gym help read one source (avoid duplicating `getHelpEntry` logic).
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — Render the description line; adjust row spacing for the three-line block; add `getDescriptionLines()`.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — Level-neutral wording for weapon catalogue descriptions.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Level-neutral wording for power-up catalogue descriptions.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §4.4.1 / §4.5 overlay description list.
- `README.md` — Update the hold-full choice / `MineralChoiceScene` description.
- Tests: `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`, `src/utils/gymHelp.test.ts`, plus a docs/description guard.

## Related work

- Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR) — introduced the detail line this item extends.
- Add 10% weighting to owned upgrades in hold-full choice (AH-0MUY47W62005FF74) — current option-selection weighting.
- Design level curves for all power-ups (AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and Weapon leveling (AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J) — supply the level/`changeSummary` data.
- PowerUps and Weapons gym scenes need a help file (AH-0MUAYB67I002REOZ) — established `getHelpEntry` as the shared catalogue-description consumer.
- Game Design Document §4.4.1 / §4.5; `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — stale copy in gym help.** Rewriting catalogue descriptions also changes the gym help overlay copy. Mitigation: update any affected help tests; keep descriptions non-empty and the AOE `/AOE/i` wording.
- **Risk — layout overflow.** Three lines per option at the current 64 px row pitch may collide. Mitigation: increase the row pitch / re-centre the block, verified by a scene test.
- **Risk — scope creep.** "Rewrite all descriptions" could balloon. Mitigation: only neutralise temporary-duration wording; do not re-tune other copy.
- **Assumption — description = item effect, summary = level delta.** The sentence describes the item as a whole; the concrete numbers for the new level remain in `changeSummary`.
- **Assumption — catalogue `description` is the correct source** (producer Q1 = B), reused rather than duplicated.
