# Intake Brief — Later-level waves collapse to the orbiting (orbital) archetype

**Work item:** AH-0MV2SGIX5005PFJT (bug, critical)
**Headline:** The auto-generated (sequenced) campaign collapses every later-level
wave onto the Phaser's `orbital` formation once a wave's difficulty target
crosses ~30, so the later game reads as "orbiting enemies" instead of the
intended varied mix. The operator reported this as enemies "circling the
player"; the player-tracking detail was **not reproducible**, but the
"once an orbital formation appears, all subsequent waves are orbital" part is
deterministic and reproduced.

## Problem statement

The shipped campaign is no longer the hand-authored `LEVELS`: since
`sequencedWavesEnabled` defaults to `true`, `PlayScene` builds every wave from
the difficulty-curve config via `buildSequencedLevels()` → `difficultySequencer.sequencer()`.
The sequencer picks a wave's composition purely by minimising the error against a
difficulty target using `enemyDifficulty`, which rates the Phaser's `orbital`
formation as the hardest (`FORMATION_KIND_ORDINAL.orbital = 5`) and the Phaser
archetype highest overall. There is **no composition / variety constraint**, so
once the target crosses ~30 the best match for *every* later wave is one or more
Phaser (`orbital`) groups. The result is a later game dominated by a single
player-relative/"special" movement archetype rather than a varied escalation.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, I want the later levels to keep introducing varied
  movement and attack styles, not to become the same orbiting formation on
  repeat."
- **Designer / content author** — "As a designer, I want the orbital Phaser to be
  a memorable one-wave set piece (E4, Level 5 'Predictable Death'), not the
  default filler for every high-difficulty wave."
- **Engineer** — "As an engineer, I want the auto-sequencer to be constrained by a
  documented, testable variety rule so this cannot silently regress."

## Existing state

- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `sequencer()` + `defaultCandidatePool()`.
  The `enemyDifficulty` factor weights live in `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`
  (`formationKind` ordinal: `single 0 → v 1 → diver 2 → rect 3 → swarm 4 →
  orbital 5`).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — merges the curve config over the static
  `LEVELS` skeleton, per-wave `curve`/`fixed`/`dynamic` modes.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` / `src/core/configStore.ts`
  (`defaultDifficultyCurves`, `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES`) — the shipped targets:
  L5W1 = 43.5, L5W2 = 62.
- `src/entities/Phaser.ts` — `applyFormationPosition` orbits the **formation
  base** (`x = baseX + R·cos θ`, `baseY` from the spawn descriptor); it does not
  reference the player.
- Precedent: `defaultCandidatePool()` already excludes `harvester`, `asteroid`
  and `grunt` because they are delivered by their own spawners
  (AH-0MUR1HZLQ001ELX9, AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6).

**Reproduction (agent, dev @ 554a4ffd).** Real `sequencer([target], defaultCandidatePool())`:

| target | composition |
|---|---|
| 10–25 | varied (`diver`/`tank`/`march`/`lane-traffic`) |
| **30–100** | **`phaser` (orbital) on every target**, + filler |

Actual shipped campaign: `L4W1 scout×18`, `L4W2 diver×18`, `L4W3 tank×18`,
`L5W1 phaser×12(orbital) + scout×18`, `L5W2 phaser×12(orbital) ×2`.

## Desired change

Constrain the auto-sequencer so a level's waves cannot collapse onto one
archetype — in particular, the `orbital` Phaser must not be selected for every
later wave. The Phaser's E4 orbital behaviour itself is intended and stays; it
should remain authorable in `fixed` waves and the gyms. The fix must be
data-driven/documented and covered by a regression test over the merged
campaign (not just the unit-level sequencer).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **No collapse (shipped campaign).** In the merged shipped campaign, no level is composed entirely of one archetype, and the `orbital`/Phaser archetype appears in **at most one wave per level**. Verified by an automated test over `buildSequencedLevels()`.
- **Documented variety rule.** The sequencer (or the campaign builder) enforces a named, documented per-level cap on archetype repetition, so a single archetype cannot fill every wave of a level. The cap is a single tunable constant/parameter, not scattered literals.
- **Regression test for the trigger.** A curve whose targets all exceed the switch threshold (≥ 30) must not produce all-orbital waves; the test pins the pre-fix failing composition and the post-fix varied one.
- **Intent preserved.** The Phaser archetype and its `orbital` behaviour are unchanged and still selectable by an authored `fixed` wave / gym scene (gym↔game parity intact).
- **Reported-but-unreproduced observation recorded.** The "enemies circle the player" observation is documented on the work item; if it recurs, capture the run seed, level/wave and enemy appearance in a follow-up.
- **Testing / validation.** Unit + integration tests cover the variety rule and the shipped-campaign invariant; **full project test suite must pass with the new changes**.
- **Documentation completeness.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §3.2 / ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION §5.1, difficulty-curve notes).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity:** the sequencer is shared; the constraint must live in the
  shared core, not be forked per scene.
- **Determinism:** `curve` waves remain seed-independent; `dynamic` waves remain
  a pure function of (curve, pool, seed). Adding the constraint must not
  reintroduce non-determinism.
- **Calibration:** the campaign remains non-decreasing in difficulty
  (`enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`) and playable; no wave may be empty or
  soft-lock (cf. the asteroid exclusion precedent).
- **No new tags/TODOs;** scope creep (e.g. re-balancing `enemyDifficulty`
  weights, the full classification system) is recorded as related work, not
  folded in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — variety/repetition constraint and/or pool
  curation.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — per-level wave composition assembly.
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — reference only (formation-kind ordinal justifies
  the runaway Phaser score).
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` / `src/core/configStore.ts` — targets may be
  retuned alongside the constraint.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` — parity for the curve-editor gym.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` —
  document the variety rule.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the operator's core concern is the *repetition* of one
  archetype across later waves ("not for all"), not the Phaser existing at all.
- **Assumption:** the "circles the player" detail was a perception (the ring
  centred near the player) or a transient state; it is not reproducible at
  `dev @ 554a4ffd`. It is recorded, not fixed here.
- **Risk:** a naive cap can starve high targets of enough threat; the fix must
  keep the campaign calibration valid (mitigation: test the shipped campaign and
  calibration).
- **Risk:** over-constraining reduces variety in the other direction; the rule
  should cap repetition, not forbid archetypes.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the "Integrate enemy classification into wave
  generation" work (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP) is the principled long-term fix; this
  item delivers a bounded, testable constraint now and references it rather than
  absorbing it.

## Related work

- AH-0MUITS0VD000DVSV — sequenced campaign builder (source of the default-on path).
- AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X — runtime auto-sequencer.
- AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT / AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B — per-wave generation modes / dynamic opening curation.
- AH-0MUR1HZLQ001ELX9 — precedent: exclude a spawner-delivered archetype from the sequencer pool.
- AH-0MT99K3FE008CT13 — E4 Phaser orbital design (intended behaviour).
- AH-0MV29NWI1007NKN7 — enemy classification (`movementClass`/`attackClass`) for balance.
- AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP — integrate classification into wave generation (blocked; depends-on AH-0MV29NWI1007NKN7).
- AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2 — add 5 levels showcasing the classic-arcade roster (paired-targeter invariant).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which observation is the one that bothered you — the Level 5 orbiting Phaser ring, the Level 4 Diver wave regrouping, both, or a different enemy?"
  — Answer (operator): "Once an orbital formation was seen *all* subsequent
  enemies were in an orbital formation. When I moved the player they moved in a
  circle around me. If I stayed still, they stayed still. They did not circle a
  fixed point. They circled me." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Can you reproduce it, and if so share the run seed / level / enemy?"
  — Answer (operator): "Not reproducible." Source: interactive reply.
- Research summary: reproduced the "all subsequent waves are orbital" behaviour
  deterministically (`sequencer()` targets ≥ 30 → Phaser/orbital); could **not**
  reproduce player-tracking (real `PlayScene` Phaser→player distance does not
  track the player; `Phaser.applyFormationPosition` orbits the formation base).
  Evidence: `.worklog/tmp/operator-clarification.md`, `src/entities/Phaser.ts:379`,
  `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts:176`.
- **OPEN QUESTION:** none — proceeding on the documented assumption that the
  actionable defect is the archetype repetition; the player-tracking detail is
  recorded for a follow-up if it recurs.

# Implement: Variety Constraint in Sequencer (AH-0MV2SGIX5005PFJT)

## Goal

Add a per-level archetype repetition cap to the sequencer so that no single enemy archetype can appear in more than MAX_ARCHETYPE_PER_LEVEL waves within a level.

## Approach

1. Add a named constant MAX_ARCHETYPE_PER_LEVEL = 1 in difficultySequencer.ts (one place, tunable).
2. Track archetype usage across waves within a level at the campaign-builder level.
3. When selecting candidates per wave, exclude archetypes that have already been used in this level up to the cap.
4. The recommended approach: enforce the constraint at the buildSequencedLevels level in sequencedLevels.ts, where the level's wave sequence is assembled. After each wave is sequenced, track archetype counts. Before sequencing the next wave, filter the candidate pool to exclude archetypes at the cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- MAX_ARCHETYPE_PER_LEVEL is a single tunable constant (default 1) in difficultySequencer.ts.
- No archetype appears in more than MAX_ARCHETYPE_PER_LEVEL waves within a level in the shipped campaign.
- The constraint does not break calibration: the campaign remains non-decreasing in difficulty (verified by enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts).
- The Phaser/orbital formation is still selectable in fixed waves and gym scenes.
- No non-determinism is introduced.

- The sequencer enforces a named documented per-level cap on archetype repetition, so a single archetype cannot fill every wave of a level, and the cap is a single tunable constant parameter not scattered literals.

## Key Files

- src/core/difficultySequencer.ts -- MAX_ARCHETYPE_PER_LEVEL constant
- src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts -- candidate pool filtering per wave
- src/data/difficulty-curves.csv -- may need minor retuning

## Goal

Add automated tests that enforce the campaign's core invariants before the new levels exist (tests will fail until Levels 6–10 are added), ensuring the plan is test-first.

## Acceptance Criteria

# Centipede appears in the plain scenes column instead of ENEMIES (AH-0MV4ZOIZR0086T66)

## Problem statement

The dedicated `GymCentipede` enemy gym scene is discovered by the generic `Gym<Name>`
glob in `GymIndex` and rendered in the left-hand **plain scenes** column. The
Centipede is an enemy archetype, so it belongs in the middle **ENEMIES** column —
exactly where the analogous `GymBoss` scene already lives — so the index no longer
miscategorises an enemy testbed as a general-purpose scene.

## Users

- **Developer browsing the gym index** — expects enemy gym scenes to be grouped in the
  ENEMIES column so an enemy testbed is launched from the correct section.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want `GymCentipede` to appear in the **ENEMIES** column so that
  every enemy testbed is grouped together on the index.
- As a **developer**, I want `GymCentipede` to appear exactly once on the index (in the
  ENEMIES column, not the plain-scene column) so I don't see a confusing, miscategorised
  entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — `GymCentipede` removed from the plain scenes column:** `GymIndex.listedScenes`
      no longer contains `{ key: 'GymCentipede', label: 'Centipede' }`, and no `Centipede`
      text row is rendered at the plain-scenes column X (`GAME_WIDTH * GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X.scenes`).
- [ ] **AC2 — `GymCentipede` surfaced as a dedicated ENEMIES row:** `GymIndex.listedEnemyScenes`
      contains `{ key: 'GymCentipede', label: 'Centipede', sceneKey: 'GymCentipede' }`, and a
      `Centipede` text row with `sceneKey === 'GymCentipede'` is rendered at the ENEMIES column X
      (`GAME_WIDTH * GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X.enemies`), alongside the existing `Fodder Enemies` and
      `Boss` rows.
- [ ] **AC3 — The ENEMIES `Centipede` row launches `GymCentipede`:** pointer-click and
      keyboard (Enter/Space) activation of the row start the `GymCentipede` scene.
- [ ] **AC4 — Tests:** `GymIndex.test.ts` is updated so the plain-scene list expectation drops
      `Centipede` and new assertions cover the ENEMIES `Centipede` row (presence, column X,
      `sceneKey`, and launch). Every existing test continues to pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code
      comments, `README.md`, and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the three-column layout and the existing column X positions (`GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X`)
  unchanged; this is a categorisation change only.
- Mirror the existing `GymBoss` exclusion/surfacing pattern in `GymIndex.ts`; do **not**
  introduce a new generic "auto-route every enemy gym to ENEMIES" mechanism (scope creep —
  see Risks).
- No behavioural change to `GymCentipede` itself (only its index visibility/labelling).
- Do **not** modify `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` — it stays a pure discovery helper; the
  column categorisation is owned by `GymIndex`.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` builds `this.entries` from
  `discoverGymScenes(loadGymSceneModules())`, filtering out `GymFodderEnemies`, `GymBoss`
  and the Dev Utilities set (`DEV_UTILITY_SCENE_KEYS`). `GymCentipede` is **not** filtered,
  so it falls through into the left plain-scenes column.
- `this.enemyEntries` is currently hard-coded to `[Fodder Enemies, Boss]`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCentipede.test.ts` asserts chain parity only; it does not assert index
  listing, so it needs no change.
- The Centipede is a **wave opt-in** (`centipede: true` in `PlayScene`), not a CSV enemy
  config, so it is not part of the `GymFodderEnemies` dropdown roster.

## Desired change

In `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`:

1. Export `CENTIPEDE_SCENE_KEY = 'GymCentipede'` and `CENTIPEDE_LABEL = 'Centipede'`
   (mirroring `BOSS_SCENE_KEY` / `BOSS_SCENE_LABEL`).
2. Add `e.key !== CENTIPEDE_SCENE_KEY` to the `this.entries` filter so the scene is excluded
   from the plain scene list.
3. Add `{ key: CENTIPEDE_SCENE_KEY, label: CENTIPEDE_LABEL, sceneKey: CENTIPEDE_SCENE_KEY }`
   to `this.enemyEntries` (placed with the other dedicated scene rows).
4. Scene registration for `scene.start(key)` is already handled by the existing
   `for (const entry of all)` loop — no change required.
5. Update the module/class doc comments that enumerate the left-column exclusions so they
   include `GymCentipede`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — Add `CENTIPEDE_SCENE_KEY` / `CENTIPEDE_LABEL`; filter
  `GymCentipede` out of `this.entries`; append the dedicated ENEMIES row; update the
  module/class doc comments describing the columns.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — Drop `Centipede` from the expected `listedScenes` list;
  assert the ENEMIES `Centipede` row (column X + `sceneKey` + launch); update the
  three-column layout test.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §Gym surface: record that `GymCentipede` is
  surfaced in the ENEMIES column and excluded from the plain scene list.
- `README.md` — §Gym Index Entry Scene: ENEMIES column roster now reads
  `Fodder Enemies`, `Boss`, `Centipede`.

## Related work

- **Boss appears in both lists on index screen (AH-0MUAYB28C004KK7X)** — established the
  precedent: exclude an enemy scene from the plain-scene column and surface a dedicated
  ENEMIES row that boots the scene directly.
- **Single enemy gym scene with in-panel enemy selector dropdown (AH-0MV13G5EV008D41E)** —
  defines the three-column index layout and the ENEMIES column semantics.
- **Centipede segmented chain (AH-0MV01EJ92008ZZ86)** — created the `GymCentipede` scene.
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** —
  sibling categorisation pattern (Dev Utilities column owns tooling scenes).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTCNZ7DN0049K73** – Scene-level tests: GymPowerUps via gameHarness (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)
- **AH-0MV2XDEKN0031KX4** – Test: gym parity intact (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: archetype, centipede, column, gym, scene (+34 more)
- `README.md` — matched: appears, archetype, centipede, column, enemies (+33 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: appears, archetype, centipede, column, currently (+30 more)

Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MV4ZOIZR0086T66.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "should be an enemy" means the `GymCentipede` **scene** belongs in the
  ENEMIES column, mirroring `GymBoss` — not that a `centipede` enemy config should be added
  to the fodder dropdown (the Centipede is a wave opt-in, not a CSV config).
- **Risk: Low.** A single-file categorisation change plus test/doc updates; no gameplay,
  entity or spawn behaviour changes.
- **Failure mode:** a `Centipede` label present in both the plain and ENEMIES columns would
  make the `findTextAt` label lookups in `GymIndex.test.ts` ambiguous — resolved by removing
  it from the plain list in the same change.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a general "auto-route every enemy gym scene to the ENEMIES column"
  mechanism is out of scope here; if wanted it should be captured as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No clarifying questions were required.** Research summary: the seed intent, combined
  with the existing `GymBoss` precedent (AH-0MUAYB28C004KK7X) and the documented three-column
  index contract (`src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  §"Gym surface", `README.md` §"Gym Index Entry Scene"), was sufficient to draft a clear
  brief. The one interpretation choice (dedicated ENEMIES **scene** row that boots
  `GymCentipede` directly, rather than adding a fodder-dropdown config) is recorded as an
  explicit documented assumption under Risks & assumptions.

It therefore reports `node: PASS` with an empty command and caches a green result without executing anything.

Impact: `implement.py finish`'s changed-scope and full-suite gates silently pass (false green), and the audit skill's `query_cached()` cannot auto-verify execution-dependent ACs from a real run.

Evidence: `run_tests.py --scope full --suite node --force --json` → `"command": ""`, `returncode: 0`, elapsed 0.04s. The real suite is `npx vitest run` (235 files / 4926 tests).

Suggested fix: add `.pi/test-config.json` with `{"suiteCommands": ["npx vitest run"], "timeoutPerCommand": 1500}` (or a test skill extension) so the runner executes and caches the real suite.

# Reduced-volume metronomic fire during the hold-full overlay

## Goal

As a player, when the hold-full power-up overlay opens I still hear my
currently active weapons firing on the exact beat at a reduced volume, with no
bullets spawned and no gameplay simulated — so the run keeps its groove.

**User story:** *As a player*, when the hold fills and the choice appears, I
still hear the ship firing on the beat (quieter, no bullets) so the game does
not feel frozen.

## Context

Parent: Hull Full overlay: metronomic fire sounds + restart countdown
(AH-0MV0QPO4N009KWVT).

- Overlay: `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`, launched after the owning scene
  pauses itself (`PlayScene.openMineralChoice()` /
  `GymFormationScene.openMineralChoice()`).
- Beat grid: `src/utils/beat.ts`; per-weapon intervals from
  `Player.getFireInterval` (Cannon 2/beat = 375 ms, Spread/Dual 1/beat =
  750 ms, Rapid 6/beat = 125 ms), phase-locked via the shared
  `CombatCoreScene.beatClock`.
- Fire cues: `PlayScene._playShootCue` → `onWeaponFired`
  (`CombatCoreScene`); cues live in `src/audio/effects.ts`; playback already
  supports a per-play `volume` (`SfxPlayOptions.volume`,
  `src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts`).

## Deliverables

- One named tunable `HOLD_FULL_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE = 0.3` (single source of
  truth, no scattered magic numbers).
- A shared `playWeaponFireSound(weaponId, options?)` helper in
  `src/audio/effects.ts` that all player weapon fire cues route through, so
  the metronome and `_playShootCue` share one path (existing cue exports
  unchanged).
- A pure, shared scheduler (in `src/scenes/core/` or `src/audio/`) that, given
  a beat clock/elapsed time, the active weapons and their intervals, emits
  on-grid cue ticks — consumed identically by `PlayScene` and every gym
  launcher. No projectiles, no gameplay simulation, no enemy cues.
- Launchers pass the active-weapon schedule into `MineralChoiceScene`, which
  drives the metronome while the overlay is open.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `playWeaponFireSound(weaponId, options?)` to `src/audio/effects.ts` and
   route `PlayScene._playShootCue` through it.
2. Add the pure scheduler deriving ticks from `src/utils/beat.ts` grid maths.
3. Add `HOLD_FULL_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` to the shared rules/constants module.
4. Extend `MineralChoiceScene.init` with a fire-schedule payload and start the
   scheduler in `create` / stop it on `select`.
5. Pass the schedule from `PlayScene.openMineralChoice` and
   `GymFormationScene.openMineralChoice`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Reduced-volume metronomic fire while paused:** When the hold-full
  overlay opens, every currently active player weapon's fire cue plays on that
  weapon's exact beat-grid cadence at **0.3× normal volume**
  (`HOLD_FULL_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`); no projectile is spawned and no gameplay
  simulation advances.
- [ ] **AC2 — Active player weapons only:** the metronomic cues cover the
  cannon and every collected timed weapon (`Player.getActiveWeapons()`), and no
  enemy cue (or other gameplay cue) plays during the overlay.
- [ ] **AC3 — Rhythm continuity / phase-lock:** the first ghost tick after the
  overlay opens lands on the beat tick the next real shot would have used and
  the cadence continues on the grid (phase preserved), asserted against
  `src/utils/beat.ts` grid maths.
- [ ] Automated tests use the recording SFX provider and a fake clock to
  assert per-weapon cadence, reduced volume and grid membership.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` and the full suite pass.

## Key Files

- `src/audio/effects.ts`
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/core/rules.ts` (or a small shared module)
- `src/utils/beat.ts` (reuse — no change expected)
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Test seams: deterministic beat-clock + recording SFX provider (first child).
